clue.text: Original Simpsons' opening that's aired at six o'clock

parts.note: original means new, not seen before

indicators.note: an opening is where something starts, so only the start of the named family is wanted

parts.note: the start of the cartoon family's name

explanation.surface: A fan recalls the cartoon's first episode going out in the early-evening slot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Simpsons was indeed first shown in an evening slot, which makes the opening look like a TV episode rather than a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening bulletin of current events is broadcast at six o'clock on British television and radio.

clue.text: Fuel component in McLaren vehicle combusted at once

indicators.note: things that burn up are broken apart and transformed, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Petrol in a racing car burns all in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: Combustion fits the engine picture so well that it reads as description, not instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: This hydrocarbon is a chief ingredient of petrol, whose rating measures how smoothly racing engines burn their fuel.

clue.text: In flight, she is a sort of attendant

indicators.note: letters in flight are scattered and flying about, so they land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a woman's job serving passengers on a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a plain definition of the whole job, hiding that the middle words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A female cabin crew member is a kind of steward who looks after passengers during air travel.

clue.text: Over time, cynic becomes Tea Party member

indicators.note: one word spread over another covers it on both sides, so the short piece sits inside

parts.note: a cynic is someone who hates or disparages
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Given time, a sceptic joins the right-wing American Tea Party movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tea Party is not the American political movement but the Mad Tea Party in Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mad Hatter is one of the guests at the Mad Tea Party in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: Biology class in which everybody is present?

definitions.text: Biology class in which everybody is present?

parts.words: Biology class in which everybody is present?
parts.note: surface reading: a school lesson with full attendance
setter's reading: a taxonomic class, and every human being belongs to it

explanation.surface: A school biology lesson with no absentees.
explanation.walkthrough: Class is a rank in biological classification; since all people are mammals, everybody is in this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The taxonomic class of warm-blooded animals that suckle their young includes humans, so every person belongs.

clue.text: Grey like the outskirts of Hinckley

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outermost letters of the place name count

parts.note: the first and last letters of the town

explanation.surface: The suburbs of Hinckley, a Leicestershire market town, are drab and grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in or coloured like burnt residue from a fire is pale grey.

clue.text: University student holds bottles of Becks

indicators.note: to bottle something is to shut it up inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: rivets means holds fast, as attention is held
U is the abbreviation for university
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A student keeps bottles of Beck's lager to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Becks looks like the German beer; here it is a northern English word for streams.
explanation.definitionFit: A beck is a small brook in northern English dialect, and small streams are also called this.

clue.text: The Church of Scotland is a constant source of annoyance
Finally Judi Dench delivered with a first-class line — it's a wrap!

indicators.note: something delivered is freed and handed over in a new form, so the letters are reworked
finally points to the very end of the actress's first name

parts.note: the last letter of the first name
taken as written
taken as written
A is the top grade, first class
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Dame Judi Dench finishes filming with a superb line, and the director calls a wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's a wrap!' is what a director says when filming ends; here it is a description of the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican tortilla rolled around a filling is literally a wrap, a cheeky reading of the film-set phrase.

clue.text: 22 Across literature introduces doubt into heart of fascist

indicators.note: to introduce one thing into another is to put it inside, so a word goes in the middle
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the political word are wanted

parts.note: the central three of its seven letters
an if is a doubt or uncertainty

explanation.surface: A literary critic finds a hint of uncertainty at the core of fascist ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 Across is a Star Trek fan, whose reading of choice is a genre of futuristic fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek enthusiasts typically read speculative futuristic fiction about space and technology.

clue.text: Guitarist/songwriter?
Fat chance of this!

parts.note: surface reading: a scornful remark that something will never happen
setter's reading: an opportunity for fat to be removed by surgery

explanation.surface: A sarcastic dismissal of some unlikely hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat chance' usually means no chance at all; read literally it is a chance concerning fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominoplasty, a cosmetic operation removing excess fat and skin from the belly, is known by this informal name.

clue.text: Notebooks, pens, erasers — essential material for poet …

indicators.note: essential material is what something is made of inside, so the answer lies within the words

parts.note: runs across the end of the first item, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A list of stationery that any working poet needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Sandy, perhaps, reaching peak during kinky sex?

indicators.note: something happening during another event falls within it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: S and M, sadomasochism
a tor is a rocky hill or peak

explanation.surface: A woman named Sandy climaxes during adventurous sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy looks like a woman's name but is the 2012 hurricane.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurricane Sandy, which struck the US east coast in 2012, is an example of a violent tempest.

clue.text: …as, for example, landlords?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the plural of the first letter of the alphabet, examples of characters
second meaning: people who let property

explanation.surface: It continues the previous clue, as if the poet's essential materials included landlords.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'as' as the plural of the letter A. The ellipsis just links the clue to the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters of the alphabet are called this, and so, punningly, are people who rent out rooms or houses.

clue.text: Redraft a better law for basic restaurant service

indicators.note: to redraft a text is to rewrite and rearrange it, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to improve legislation on the minimum standard of service in restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain bottled or tap drinking water served with a meal is the most basic thing a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Training base for space program

indicators.note: in a down answer a base sits underneath, so the first piece goes below the second

parts.note: the sky is the space above us
PE is physical education, training in school

explanation.surface: A launch site for astronaut training in a space programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Program' with the American spelling is a computer program, not a space programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Skype is a software application for internet video calls, a computer program.

clue.text: Brown mineral found outside 8

indicators.note: one thing found outside another wraps around it

parts.note: ore is mineral rock mined for metal
8 Down is the Scottish church, and CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A brown mineral deposit is discovered beside a Scottish church.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown and mineral seem to go together, but only the colour is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earthy pigment, so the word names a brownish colour.

clue.text: Short break in endless celebration that takes place on Oahu

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
a short version of something is missing its end

parts.note: an honour is a celebration of someone

indicators.note: without an end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lull is a short pause or break

explanation.surface: A brief pause in a never-ending Hawaiian party.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces lose their last letter before one goes inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu, the capital of Hawaii, is located on the island of Oahu.

clue.text: Discarding instant coffee for a different drink

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away, so part of the word is removed

parts.note: mocha is a type of coffee
a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: Someone gives up instant coffee in favour of another beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Instant coffee looks like one item, but instant is a separate piece. Cha is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha, or char, is a British slang word for tea, a beverage other than coffee.

clue.text: It's a grave situation to sport comb over at American college

indicators.note: to sport is to wear, and in a down answer what is worn sits on top
turned over means flipped, so these words read backwards

parts.note: at as written, A for American, C for college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student wearing a comb-over at an American college is in a serious predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb over' looks like the hairstyle, but over belongs to the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground burial galleries are literally places for graves, a pun on a grave, serious situation.

clue.text: Head of business at BSkyB regularly entertained big authoritarian

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece goes inside
the head of a word is its front, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter
OS is outsize, the clothing size meaning big

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter of the company name is used

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: The chief of the satellite broadcaster BSkyB hosted a powerful tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bossy person domineers and gives orders, behaving in an authoritarian manner.

clue.text: Watch some games of 27, perhaps — that's the attitude!

parts.note: to mind is to watch or look after
27 is the Swedish tennis player, and a set is a group of games in tennis

explanation.surface: Watching a tennis star play brings out the right competitive spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed way of thinking about something is one's outlook, approach or attitude.

clue.text: In the end, Capt. 8 transported with ease, said one of his lovers?

indicators.note: transported means carried off and moved, so the letters are moved around
the end of the abbreviated rank means its last letter

parts.note: the last letter
the solution to 8 Down, here the captain of the Enterprise

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: spoken, the word sounds like the plural of the letter E

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk is beamed away effortlessly, says one of his many conquests.
explanation.walkthrough: Lovers seems to mean the captain's romantic partners; it means fans who love his show.
explanation.definitionFit: A devoted fan of Star Trek loves Captain Kirk's show, so is one of his lovers in a playful sense.

clue.text: Saint Thomas Aquinas initially skirted point over issue of Latin translation

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go around its edge, so the outer letters wrap the rest
initially points to the first letters of the theologian's two names

parts.note: the first letters of each name
E is east, a compass point
res is the Latin word for a thing, matter or issue

explanation.surface: Aquinas sidestepped a point about a matter of translating Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the point sits over the Latin word. The Saint in the surface is Aquinas, but the definition names a different saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Teresa of Ávila, the Spanish mystic, is one famous holder of this name, as is Mother Teresa.

clue.text: Assassinated Kennedy then led away as one at 8 might be

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: assassinated means murdered
taken as written
Ted Kennedy, the US senator

explanation.surface: A Kennedy was assassinated and then carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: Kennedy suggests JFK, but the brother needed is Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending the Scottish church might well wear the traditional tartan skirt of Highland dress.

clue.text: Panda possibly caught chill before visiting Arctic Circle?

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's place, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: the Arctic Circle is one of the two polar circles
to ice is to chill
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A panda catches a cold on a trip to the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda car is British slang for a small police patrol car, once painted in panda-like blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a panda car is an informal name for a patrol vehicle, so a panda is one example.

clue.text: Hotpoint cracked revolutionary Orange product

explanation.walkthrough: Hotpoint is a British appliance brand and Orange a former British phone network, so the surface suggests a broken washing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The white spongy layer under the peel of a citrus fruit is part of what an orange produces.

clue.text: Fuel from McLaren's second vehicle, perhaps

parts.note: surface padding: a McLaren is a racing car, an example of the vehicle that follows
a car is one kind of vehicle
B is second, as in a second grade or class

explanation.surface: Petrol taken from a spare racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: Fuel suggests petrol, but here it is the food that fuels the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for carbohydrate, the nutrient the body burns for energy, often eaten by athletes before exercise.

clue.text: Impromptu bail out over Germany

indicators.note: out of order means disarranged, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: An unplanned parachute jump over Germany.

clue.text: Tennis player of questionable gender?

wordplay.note: a person of uncertain sex is a boy or a girl

explanation.surface: Speculation about the sex of a tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: Gender questions in tennis call up famous controversies, but the wordplay is just the abbreviations for boy and girl joined by 'or'.
explanation.definitionFit: Björn Borg, the Swedish champion, won Wimbledon five times in a row.

clue.text: Workman stripping out large ship's guidance system

parts.note: the tiller is the handle that steers a boat
L is the abbreviation for large

clue.text: Think about Kilmarnock's first division airing of Norman Hunter?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to muse is to think

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of the Scottish town

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: airing a word means voicing it, so it is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tier is a level or division

explanation.surface: A pundit muses on Kilmarnock in the top league and the tough-tackling footballer Norman Hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Hunter was a famously hard Leeds United defender; read as words, a Norman hunter is a French gunman.
